evidence.quote: At Rhein-Waal University of Applied Sciences, you do not pay tuition fees, as it is a state university in North Rhine-Westphalia.
Did you complete your school-leaving qualifications outside of Germany? If so, you’ll need to apply via uni-assist.

value.quotedAs: Proof of sufficient English language proficiency

evidence.quote: University entrance qualification obtained in Germany (e.g. the German Abitur): Proof is usually provided by your school leaving certificate.
Proof of sufficient English language proficiency for English-taught degree programmes

notes: Tuition for non-EU/foreign-diploma applicants: the programme page and the central cost page state that no tuition fees are charged at this state university; the DAAD entry says 'Tuition fees per semester None'. The applicant still pays a semester contribution (about 300 EUR per semester per DAAD; the cost page mentions only a semester fee and a Germany Ticket), which is not tuition and is not included in the tuition figure. Deadline: the pages give only day and month ('15 July') without a year, so it is recorded as a recurring deadline; both pages say it applies to applicants from all countries / winter semester intake. Application channel: uni-assist is stated for applicants with school-leaving qualifications from outside Germany (de-uni-assist); the pages do not mention a separate VPD / preliminary review, so de-uni-assist-vpd was not used. Documents: only the school leaving certificate and proof of English proficiency are named in the enrolment/application document lists; no translation requirement is stated on the pages. The accepted English tests are listed as examples ('e.g.') with UNIcert II, telc, TOEIC, PTE Academic, Cambridge, TOEFL iBT and IELTS Academic; the B2 certificate may alternatively be replaced by school certificates showing seven years of English lessons, which is a manual check.
